match.reason: The closest bank point, eco-law-demand, teaches the law of demand and movement along the curve but never explains why demand falls, while the new point's core is the income and substitution effects, and e-demand gives a different reason (diminishing marginal utility), so the card would need a new step.

draft.title: The law of demand
card: The law of demand says that, other things being equal, a fall in price raises the quantity demanded and a rise in price lowers it. The demand curve slopes downwards.
Income effect
when a price rises, the same income buys less, so buying power falls. Consumers buy a smaller quantity of that good.
Substitution effect
when a price rises, other goods become relatively cheaper. Consumers switch some of their spending to those goods.
A change in the good's own price causes a movement along the demand curve. It does not shift the curve.
draft.remember: A higher price cuts buying power and makes other goods look cheaper, so quantity demanded falls.

a.q: The price of pasta rises, and Ravi buys rice instead because it is now relatively cheaper. Which effect is this?
opts: The substitution effect
The income effect
A shift of the demand curve
A fall in consumer confidence
a.why: Ravi switches to another good that looks cheaper compared with pasta, which is the substitution effect. It is not the income effect, which is about buying power shrinking when a price rises.
a.clue: Ravi changes to a different good.

b.q: The price of train tickets in Geelong rises. Hana's wage is unchanged, so she can now afford fewer trips and cuts her travel. Which explanation and result fit?
opts: Income effect, a movement along the demand curve
Substitution effect, a movement along the demand curve
Income effect, a shift of the demand curve
Substitution effect, a shift of the demand curve
b.why: Hana's buying power has fallen because the same wage buys fewer tickets, which is the income effect. The cause is the good's own price, so it is a movement along the curve, not a shift. Hana does not switch to another good, so it is not the substitution effect.
b.clue: Is Hana switching goods, or is her buying power shrinking?

b.best: Income effect, a movement along the demand curve

a.q: The price of pasta rises while the price of rice stays the same. Ravi buys less pasta and more rice. Which effect explains his change?
opts: The substitution effect
The income effect
A shift of the pasta demand curve
A rise in Ravi's buying power
a.why: Rice now costs less compared with pasta, so Ravi moves some spending from pasta to rice. That is the substitution effect. The income effect would show up as Ravi buying less because his money stretches less far, not as a switch to another good.
a.clue: Ravi changes to a different good.
